text:
customer-jane: Hey team — we flipped traffic to the PrivateLink endpoint this morning and started seeing intermittent 503s from the Redwood API (only via the private endpoint). Public endpoint still fine.

maria_support: Sorry about the disruption. Can you paste the curl -v output and a dig for the api host? Also any proxy or egress appliances on your side?

customer-jane: Sure — we route egress through a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy. Here are quick repros:
```
$ dig +short api.prod.redwood.internal
vpce-abc123-xyz.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com

$ curl -v https://api.prod.redwood.internal/v1/health
* Connected to vpce-abc123-xyz.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com (10.1.2.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, server accepted to use h2
* TLS 1.2 connection established
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.prod.redwood.internal
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
>
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< Server: nginx
< Content-Type: text/html
< Content-Length: 131
< 
503 Service Unavailable
```

maria_support: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) can you run openssl s_client -servername api.prod.redwood.internal -connect <vpce-ip>:443 and paste the cert subject/SANs? 2) can you confirm whether the corporate proxy is doing full TLS termination (i.e., presenting its own cert) vs transparent TCP passthrough?

customer-jane: openssl shows the proxy's cert (CN=corp-proxy.internal), not Redwood's cert. So proxy is intercepting. We added the PrivateLink DNS and the traffic lands at the VPCE ENI, but our proxy is still terminating TLS first.

alex_sre: That explains a lot. If the TLS-intercepting proxy terminates and rewrites Host headers or SNI, the backend routing on our side (we route by SNI/Host to tenant clusters) can misroute or send traffic to a pool without healthy targets. ALBs/NLBs will then return 503 when no healthy targets exist. Can you capture a request/response pair or tcpdump showing the Host header from the proxy to the VPCE? Short repro steps suffice.

customer-jane: Grabbed a request trace from the proxy — it replaces the Host with the upstream internal name and injects its own client cert. Snippet:
```
Host: internal-backend.prod
X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.22
TLS Client Cert: CN=corp-proxy
```

alex_sre: Yep that's it. Two remediation options:
- Add api.prod.redwood.internal (and any Redwood hostnames) to your proxy bypass/allowlist so TLS is end-to-end to our endpoint (preserves SNI/Host). OR
- Configure the proxy to preserve original Host and SNI and avoid rewriting upstream Host headers and not terminate at the proxy (less recommended).

maria_support: For immediate mitigation, adding the domain to the proxy bypass fixed this for a different customer. Can you try adding a bypass rule and test? Also confirm no SG/network ACLs are blocking ephemeral ports (we use normal client ephemeral ranges for upstream connections) — but given the cert/proxy evidence, proxy bypass is higher priority.

customer-jane: I pushed a bypass rule for api.prod.redwood.internal and tested — no 503s in the last 30m. Rolling this change to prod now. Thanks!

alex_sre: Great. Follow-ups: if you need to keep TLS intercept for auditing, add an allowlist for the PrivateLink CIDR or a specific path to do TCP passthrough for that host. We'll also add a note to our PrivateLink troubleshooting doc about TLS-intercept proxies causing 503s due to SNI/Host rewrite.

infra_bot: deploy:ticket-4321 created -> doc update + private-link-runbook entry queued.

customer-jane: Appreciate the quick help :heart:
